title: SENTRY Onboarding Curriculum Live Term Ledger

audit_laws.O1_calibration: Every technical term is introduced as analogy -> plain definition -> term, at FIRST USE.
audit_laws.zero_prior_use: No technical term appears in Station 01 before its formal definition in Station 02.
audit_laws.connective_tissue: Every term specifies a where_you_meet_it_next pointer to downstream stations.

terms.first_use_section: Cluster 1: The Web & How Programs Talk
terms.analogy: The kitchen, pantry, and dishwashing line of a 24-hour restaurant.
terms.plain_definition: A dedicated computer that stays awake day and night waiting to fulfill requests from other computers and deliver answers back.
terms.in_sentry: The Python application running on port 8000 that inspects email headers, calculates threat scores, and builds PDF reports.
terms.memory_hook: Servers serve; they do the heavy lifting in the back.

terms.first_use_section: Cluster 1: The Web & How Programs Talk
terms.analogy: The restaurant diner sitting in a booth reading the laminated menu.
terms.plain_definition: The visual program, phone app, or web browser that a human being interacts with directly.
terms.in_sentry: The web browser running on port 3000 that displays the dark-themed analyst dashboard, maps, and network graphs.
terms.memory_hook: Clients ask; servers answer.

terms.first_use_section: Cluster 1: The Web & How Programs Talk
terms.analogy: The engine block, pistons, and transmission hidden under the locked hood of a sports car.
terms.plain_definition: All the mathematical calculations, database queries, and behind-the-scenes logic that power an app out of human sight.
terms.in_sentry: The 82 files in the backend/ directory containing Python code for machine learning, forensic header parsing, and cryptographic checks.
terms.memory_hook: Backend is the brain; frontend is the face.

terms.first_use_section: Cluster 1: The Web & How Programs Talk
terms.analogy: The car's steering wheel, glowing speedometer, gas pedal, and touchscreen display.
terms.plain_definition: Everything you can see, click, hover over, or type into on your computer screen.
terms.in_sentry: The React and TypeScript code in frontend/src/ that draws interactive severity badges, dynamic graph nodes, and map markers.
terms.memory_hook: If your mouse can click it, it's frontend.

terms.first_use_section: Cluster 1: The Web & How Programs Talk
terms.analogy: The restaurant waiter taking orders from the table to the kitchen and bringing food back.
terms.plain_definition: A formal, agreed-upon messenger system that lets two completely different computer programs communicate and exchange data securely.
terms.in_sentry: The bridge connecting the React frontend to the Python backend over HTTP.
terms.memory_hook: The messenger and order-taker between programs.

terms.first_use_section: Cluster 1: The Web & How Programs Talk
terms.analogy: A specific labeled counter at the post office (Window 1 for stamps, Window 2 for parcels).
terms.plain_definition: A specific web address (URL) dedicated to performing one exact task and returning one exact type of data.
terms.in_sentry: The 29 registered endpoints (24 business forensic routes + 5 system routes) in FastAPI.
terms.memory_hook: One specific doorway for one specific job.

terms.analogy: A fireproof digital filing cabinet in the detective squad room with labeled drawers.
terms.plain_definition: A specialized program built to store, organize, search, and retrieve structured information permanently.
terms.in_sentry: The SQLite database file (backend/sentry.db) storing emails, IOCs, and hash chain blocks.
terms.memory_hook: Where data sleeps safely between computer restarts.

terms.analogy: A rigid pre-printed customs declaration form where every box has strict rules.
terms.plain_definition: The blueprint or contract that strictly defines what fields and types data must have.
terms.in_sentry: Pydantic models in backend/app/schemas/ validating every email and report structure.
terms.memory_hook: The rigid cookie-cutter that data must fit into.

terms.analogy: A pilot's laminated pre-flight checklist verifying every instrument before takeoff.
terms.plain_definition: A separate piece of code written to run the main software with known inputs and check outputs.
terms.in_sentry: The 164 automated pytest cases running across 26 test modules in backend/tests/.
terms.memory_hook: Software checking software so humans don't have to guess.

terms.analogy: Testing an individual headlight bulb on a workbench before installing it into a car.
terms.plain_definition: A test that isolates a single, small function and checks whether it works in complete isolation.
terms.in_sentry: Testing just the IP address special-use validator without starting the server.
terms.memory_hook: Testing one single brick, not the whole building.

terms.analogy: An automated automotive crash-test barrier certifying vehicle safety before road release.
terms.plain_definition: An end-to-end robotic test rig that boots the entire system, executes real actions, and gates release.
terms.in_sentry: tools/verify_sentry.py executing all 21 operational gates with Playwright browser automation.
terms.memory_hook: The unbribable electronic inspector.

terms.analogy: The master blueprint safe in an architect's office containing all drawings and revisions.
terms.plain_definition: The central folder containing all project code, documentation, test suites, and history.
terms.in_sentry: The SENTRY root directory tracking exactly 551 files.
terms.memory_hook: The project's permanent home address.

terms.analogy: A video game save-point system that never overwrites old saves.
terms.plain_definition: A version control tool recording every modification made to files over time, tracking who and why.
terms.in_sentry: The tool tracking all commits, tags, and branches across the repository.
terms.memory_hook: The time machine for software projects.

terms.analogy: A parallel drafting table where an author drafts a chapter without touching the book.
terms.plain_definition: An isolated copy of a codebase in Git where changes are developed safely.
terms.in_sentry: Feature branches like feat/master-email-verification or docs/onboarding-guide.
terms.memory_hook: A safe sandbox detour off the main highway.

terms.analogy: Submitting a newly written chapter to the editor-in-chief for formal line-by-line review.
terms.plain_definition: A formal proposal on GitHub to merge code from a branch into main with review and test results.
terms.in_sentry: PRs #14, #15, #16 landing features sequentially under automated gate inspection.
terms.memory_hook: "Here is my proposed work — please inspect and merge."

terms.analogy: An automated quality-control conveyor belt inspecting every manufactured part before shipping.
terms.plain_definition: An automated cloud robot that runs the test suite, linters, and security checks on every push.
terms.in_sentry: GitHub Actions workflow running 6 matrix jobs across Python and Node.
terms.memory_hook: The tireless robot that tests your work every time you save.

terms.analogy: A standard steel shipping container loaded with a machine and its generator that runs anywhere.
terms.plain_definition: A lightweight self-contained software package bundling an app and all its dependencies.
terms.in_sentry: Production multi-arch container images published to GitHub Container Registry.
terms.memory_hook: An entire application packed into an identical suitcase.

terms.analogy: The global port authority crane and tractor system moving and running containers worldwide.
terms.plain_definition: The software engine and platform used to build, share, and run containers.
terms.in_sentry: Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml enabling one-command enterprise boots.
terms.memory_hook: The engine that powers the container world.

terms.analogy: Unlocking the front doors and turning on the neon OPEN sign of a new store on opening day.
terms.plain_definition: Moving finished software into the live operational environment for real users.
terms.in_sentry: Executing demo_day.ps1 or launching GHCR production images.
terms.memory_hook: Flipping the switch from "under construction" to "live."

terms.analogy: A human fingerprint or barcode derived mathematically from physical ridges.
terms.plain_definition: A mathematical calculation converting any text or file into a fixed-length string.
terms.in_sentry: Condensing an entire 45KB raw email into an exact 64-character digital fingerprint.
terms.memory_hook: One unique digital fingerprint for every document.

terms.analogy: A tamper-evident cryptographic wax seal: if one comma changes, the seal shatters visibly.
terms.plain_definition: A military-grade hashing algorithm (NIST standard) producing an unforgeable 64-character hex code.
terms.in_sentry: Used to seal raw emails in evidence_vault/ and link custody blocks.
terms.memory_hook: The unbreakable gold standard of digital wax seals.

terms.analogy: The contacts app on your phone translating human names to phone numbers.
terms.plain_definition: The internet's phonebook translating human names (apexbank.com) into computer IPs (203.0.113.9).
terms.in_sentry: Looking up domain authority and authorized mail transfer servers.
terms.memory_hook: The internet's phonebook.

terms.analogy: The 3 anti-counterfeit passport features: guest list (SPF), holographic seal (DKIM), border rules (DMARC).
terms.plain_definition: The three standard authentication protocols verifying if an email genuinely came from its claimed sender.
terms.in_sentry: Evaluated in Header Forensics; failure raises the threat floor to 0.85 CRITICAL.
terms.memory_hook: The digital passport and visa stamps of email.

terms.analogy: An angler dangling shiny plastic bait on a sharp hook waiting for a fish to bite.
terms.plain_definition: An attack where an adversary poses as a trusted entity to steal passwords or financial data.
terms.in_sentry: Primary classification label identifying fake banking alerts and credential harvesting forms.
terms.memory_hook: Fake bait designed to steal your confidential keys.

terms.analogy: An imposter wearing the CEO's tailored suit quietly ordering finance to wire emergency funds.
terms.plain_definition: A targeted email attack impersonating executives to divert funds, containing zero malware or links.
terms.in_sentry: Detected via linguistic urgency, executive authority signals, and lookalike domain checks.
terms.memory_hook: The corporate imposter whispering fraudulent wire instructions.

terms.analogy: A stranger promising a chest of gold if you lend them $50 for the padlock key right now.
terms.plain_definition: A scam promising a massive windfall in exchange for a small upfront administrative fee.
terms.in_sentry: Specialized classification subtype ADVANCE-FEE FRAUD with dedicated response playbooks.
terms.memory_hook: Pay a small fee now to unlock a fortune that doesn't exist.

terms.analogy: Muddy boot prints, a broken latch, and a dropped receipt left behind by a burglar.
terms.plain_definition: Technical evidence left behind on a network or computer that positively identifies malicious activity.
terms.in_sentry: The standardized 4-row technical evidence table: Sender IP, Sender Domain, Reply-To, Reply-To Domain.
terms.memory_hook: The digital clues left behind at the crime scene.

terms.analogy: The signed paper log on a police evidence locker proving the weapon was never altered.
terms.plain_definition: A chronological, tamper-evident record proving evidence was never altered from discovery to court trial.
terms.in_sentry: RFC 3227 mathematical hash chain linking raw email genesis to every forensic enrichment step.
terms.memory_hook: The legal diary proving evidence was never tampered with.

terms.analogy: A nuclear submarine submerged beneath polar ice operating with zero cables to shore.
terms.plain_definition: A computer system physically isolated from unsecured public networks and the internet.
terms.in_sentry: Certified appliance mode running 100% offline with local databases and zero external daemons.
terms.memory_hook: Complete security through physical and digital isolation.

terms.analogy: A nightclub bouncer scanning the line: "No sandals, valid photo ID required" — an instant rule.
terms.plain_definition: A practical rule-of-thumb shortcut used to make fast, reliable decisions without complex math.
terms.in_sentry: Layer 1 deterministic rules catching Tor exit nodes and hard authentication failures in <1ms.
terms.memory_hook: A fast common-sense rule written by human experts.
